cues.zh: 我很兴奋地想和大家分享
cues.en: I'm really excited to share with you

cues.zh: 一些让我非常惊讶的发现
cues.en: some findings that really surprise me

cues.zh: 关于是什么让公司最成功，
cues.en: about what makes companies succeed the most,

cues.zh: 哪些因素对创业成功真正最重要。
cues.en: what factors actually matter the most for startup success.

cues.zh: 我相信创业组织
cues.en: I believe that the startup organization

cues.zh: 是让世界变得更美好的最伟大形式之一。
cues.en: is one of the greatest forms to make the world a better place.

cues.zh: 如果你把一群有合适股权激励的人
cues.en: If you take a group of people with the right equity incentives

cues.zh: 组织成一家创业公司，
cues.en: and organize them in a startup,

cues.zh: 你就能以前所未有的方式释放人类潜能。
cues.en: you can unlock human potential in a way never before possible.

cues.zh: 你让他们实现难以置信的成就。
cues.en: You get them to achieve unbelievable things.

cues.zh: 但如果创业组织这么伟大，
cues.en: But if the startup organization is so great,

cues.zh: 为什么这么多会失败？
cues.en: why do so many fail?

cues.zh: 这就是我想弄清楚的。
cues.en: That's what I wanted to find out.

cues.zh: 我想找出真正最重要的是什么
cues.en: I wanted to find out what actually matters most

cues.zh: 对创业成功而言。
cues.en: for startup success.

cues.zh: 而且我想尽量系统地去做，
cues.en: And I wanted to try to be systematic about it,

cues.zh: 避免我的一些直觉，也许还有我的误解
cues.en: avoid some of my instincts and maybe misperceptions I have

cues.zh: 来自我多年来见过的这么多公司。
cues.en: from so many companies I've seen over the years.

cues.zh: 我想弄清楚这件事
cues.en: I wanted to know this

cues.zh: 因为我从12岁起就开始创业
cues.en: because I've been starting businesses since I was 12 years old

cues.zh: 初中时在公交站卖糖果，
cues.en: when I sold candy at the bus stop in junior high school,

cues.zh: 高中时做太阳能装置，
cues.en: to high school, when I made solar energy devices,

cues.zh: 大学时做扬声器。
cues.en: to college, when I made loudspeakers.

cues.zh: 大学毕业后，我开始创办软件公司。
cues.en: And when I graduated from college, I started software companies.

cues.zh: 20年前，我创办了Idealab，
cues.en: And 20 years ago, I started Idealab,

cues.zh: 过去20年里，我们创办了100多家公司，
cues.en: and in the last 20 years, we started more than 100 companies,

cues.zh: 有很多成功，也有很多惨痛的失败。
cues.en: many successes, and many big failures.

cues.zh: 我们从那些失败中学到了很多。
cues.en: We learned a lot from those failures.

cues.zh: 所以我试着去审视哪些因素
cues.en: So I tried to look across what factors

cues.zh: 对公司成败影响最大。
cues.en: accounted the most for company success and failure.

cues.zh: 我看了这五个因素。
cues.en: So I looked at these five.

cues.zh: 第一，想法。
cues.en: First, the idea.

cues.zh: 我以前认为想法就是一切。
cues.en: I used to think that the idea was everything.

cues.zh: 我把公司命名为Idealab，就是因为我太崇拜
cues.en: I named my company Idealab for how much I worship

cues.zh: 你最初想出点子时那“啊哈！”的一刻。
cues.en: the "aha!" moment when you first come up with the idea.

cues.zh: 但后来，
cues.en: But then over time,

cues.zh: 我开始觉得，或许团队、执行力、适应能力，
cues.en: I came to think that maybe the team, the execution, adaptability,

cues.zh: 这些比点子更重要。
cues.en: that mattered even more than the idea.

cues.zh: 我从没想过会在TED舞台上引用拳击手Mike Tyson的话，
cues.en: I never thought I'd be quoting boxer Mike Tyson on the TED stage,

cues.zh: 但他曾说过，
cues.en: but he once said,

cues.zh: “每个人都有计划，直到脸上挨了一拳。”（笑声）
cues.en: "Everybody has a plan, until they get punched in the face." (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我觉得这话在商业上也同样成立。
cues.en: And I think that's so true about business as well.

cues.zh: 团队的执行力，很大程度上
cues.en: So much about a team's execution

cues.zh: 就在于能否适应被客户迎面痛击。
cues.en: is its ability to adapt to getting punched in the face by the customer.

cues.zh: 客户才是真正的现实。
cues.en: The customer is the true reality.

cues.zh: 所以我才开始认为，
cues.en: And that's why I came to think

cues.zh: 团队或许才是最重要的。
cues.en: that the team maybe was the most important thing.

cues.zh: 然后我开始关注商业模式。
cues.en: Then I started looking at the business model.

cues.zh: 公司是否有非常清晰的路径来创造客户收入？
cues.en: Does the company have a very clear path generating customer revenues?

cues.zh: 这一点开始在我思考成功最关键因素时
cues.en: That started rising to the top in my thinking

cues.zh: 上升到首位。
cues.en: about maybe what mattered most for success.

cues.zh: 然后我看了融资情况。
cues.en: Then I looked at the funding.

cues.zh: 有时公司会获得巨额融资。
cues.en: Sometimes companies received intense amounts of funding.

cues.zh: 也许那才是最重要的？
cues.en: Maybe that's the most important thing?

cues.zh: 然后当然还有时机。
cues.en: And then of course, the timing.

cues.zh: 这个想法是不是太超前，世界还没准备好？
cues.en: Is the idea way too early and the world's not ready for it?

cues.zh: 是偏早，也就是说你领先一步，得去教育市场？
cues.en: Is it early, as in, you're in advance and you have to educate the world?

cues.zh: 还是刚刚好？
cues.en: Is it just right?

cues.zh: 或者已经太晚，竞争对手已经太多了？
cues.en: Or is it too late, and there's already too many competitors?

cues.zh: 所以我试着非常仔细地考察这五个因素
cues.en: So I tried to look very carefully at these five factors

cues.zh: 横跨许多公司。
cues.en: across many companies.

cues.zh: 我考察了所有100家Idealab公司，
cues.en: And I looked across all 100 Idealab companies,

cues.zh: 以及100家非Idealab公司
cues.en: and 100 non-Idealab companies

cues.zh: 想从中得出一些科学性的结论。
cues.en: to try and come up with something scientific about it.

cues.zh: 先说这些Idealab公司，
cues.en: So first, on these Idealab companies,

cues.zh: 排名前五的公司——
cues.en: the top five companies --

cues.zh: Citysearch、CarsDirect、GoTo、NetZero、Tickets.com——
cues.en: Citysearch, CarsDirect, GoTo, NetZero, Tickets.com --

cues.zh: 它们都成了十亿美元级的成功案例。
cues.en: those all became billion-dollar successes.

cues.zh: 排在最后的五家公司——
cues.en: And the five companies on the bottom --

cues.zh: Z.com、Insider Pages、MyLife、Desktop Factory、Peoplelink——
cues.en: Z.com, Insider Pages, MyLife, Desktop Factory, Peoplelink --

cues.zh: 我们都曾寄予厚望，但没能成功。
cues.en: we all had high hopes for, but didn't succeed.

cues.zh: 于是我试着按所有这些维度来排序
cues.en: So I tried to rank across all of those attributes

cues.zh: 看看这些公司在各个维度上表现如何。
cues.en: how I felt those companies scored on each of those dimensions.

cues.zh: 然后对于非 Idealab 的公司，我研究了那些大获成功的案例，
cues.en: And then for non-Idealab companies, I looked at wild successes,

cues.zh: 比如 Airbnb、Instagram、Uber、Youtube 和 LinkedIn。
cues.en: like Airbnb and Instagram and Uber and Youtube and LinkedIn.

cues.zh: 还有一些失败的：
cues.en: And some failures:

cues.zh: Webvan、Kozmo、Pets.com
cues.en: Webvan, Kozmo, Pets.com

cues.zh: Flooz 和 Friendster。
cues.en: Flooz and Friendster.

cues.zh: 垫底的那些公司融资规模很大，
cues.en: The bottom companies had intense funding,

cues.zh: 有些甚至还有商业模式，
cues.en: they even had business models in some cases,

cues.zh: 但它们没能成功。
cues.en: but they didn't succeed.

cues.zh: 我试着找出在所有这些问题公司中，
cues.en: I tried to look at what factors actually accounted the most

cues.zh: 真正最能解释成败的因素，
cues.en: for success and failure across all of these companies,

cues.zh: 结果让我非常惊讶。
cues.en: and the results really surprised me.

cues.zh: 排在第一位的因素是时机。
cues.en: The number one thing was timing.

cues.zh: 时机占了42%，
cues.en: Timing accounted for 42 percent

cues.zh: 是成功与失败之间的差异。
cues.en: of the difference between success and failure.

cues.zh: 团队和执行排在第二，
cues.en: Team and execution came in second,

cues.zh: 而想法，
cues.en: and the idea,

cues.zh: 想法的可差异化、想法的独特性，
cues.en: the differentiability of the idea, the uniqueness of the idea,

cues.zh: 实际上排在第三。
cues.en: that actually came in third.

cues.zh: 当然，这并非绝对定论，
cues.en: Now, this isn't absolutely definitive,

cues.zh: 这并不是说想法不重要，
cues.en: it's not to say that the idea isn't important,

cues.zh: 但让我非常惊讶的是，想法竟然不是最重要的东西。
cues.en: but it very much surprised me that the idea wasn't the most important thing.

cues.zh: 有时候，时机把握得好反而更重要。
cues.en: Sometimes it mattered more when it was actually timed.

cues.zh: 最后两项，商业模式和资金，我其实觉得挺合理。
cues.en: The last two, business model and funding, made sense to me actually.

cues.zh: 我认为商业模式排在那么低是有道理的，
cues.en: I think business model makes sense to be that low

cues.zh: 因为你可以一开始没有商业模式，
cues.en: because you can start out without a business model

cues.zh: 如果客户对你创造的东西有需求，之后再补上。
cues.en: and add one later if your customers are demanding what you're creating.

cues.zh: 而资金，我也觉得，
cues.en: And funding, I think as well,

cues.zh: 如果你一开始资金不足，但正在获得增长势头，
cues.en: if you're underfunded at first but you're gaining traction,

cues.zh: 尤其是在当今时代，
cues.en: especially in today's age,

cues.zh: 获得大量融资是非常非常容易的。
cues.en: it's very, very easy to get intense funding.

cues.zh: 那我现在给你们举几个具体例子，分别对应这几点。
cues.en: So now let me give you some specific examples about each of these.

cues.zh: 就拿Airbnb这种家喻户晓的大获成功来说。
cues.en: So take a wild success like Airbnb that everybody knows about.

cues.zh: 这家公司 famously 被许多聪明投资人拒绝过
cues.en: Well, that company was famously passed on by many smart investors

cues.zh: 因为人们觉得，
cues.en: because people thought,

cues.zh: “没人会把自己家的空间租给陌生人。”
cues.en: "No one's going to rent out a space in their home to a stranger."

cues.zh: 当然，人们证明这是错的。
cues.en: Of course, people proved that wrong.

cues.zh: 但它成功的原因之一，
cues.en: But one of the reasons it succeeded,

cues.zh: 除了好的商业模式、好点子、出色的执行，
cues.en: aside from a good business model, a good idea, great execution,

cues.zh: 还有时机。
cues.en: is the timing.

cues.zh: 这家公司恰好在经济衰退最严重的时候出现
cues.en: That company came out right during the height of the recession

cues.zh: 那时人们真的需要额外收入，
cues.en: when people really needed extra money,

cues.zh: 这也许帮人们克服了
cues.en: and that maybe helped people overcome

cues.zh: 把自家房子租给陌生人的抵触心理。
cues.en: their objection to renting out their own home to a stranger.

cues.zh: Uber也是一样。
cues.en: Same thing with Uber.

cues.zh: Uber出现时，
cues.en: Uber came out,

cues.zh: 是家了不起的公司，商业模式了不起，
cues.en: incredible company, incredible business model,

cues.zh: 执行也很出色。
cues.en: great execution, too.

cues.zh: 但时机恰到好处
cues.en: But the timing was so perfect

cues.zh: 正好赶上他们需要把司机纳入系统的需求。
cues.en: for their need to get drivers into the system.

cues.zh: 司机们当时在找外快；这非常非常重要。
cues.en: Drivers were looking for extra money; it was very, very important.

cues.zh: 我们早期的一些成功，比如Citysearch，正好出现在人们需要网页的时候。
cues.en: Some of our early successes, Citysearch, came out when people needed web pages.

cues.zh: GoTo.com，我们其实1998年在TED上就发布了，
cues.en: GoTo.com, which we announced actually at TED in 1998,

cues.zh: 当时企业正在寻找高性价比的引流方式。
cues.en: was when companies were looking for cost-effective ways to get traffic.

cues.zh: 我们觉得这个想法太棒了，
cues.en: We thought the idea was so great,

cues.zh: 但实际上，时机可能更重要。
cues.en: but actually, the timing was probably maybe more important.

cues.zh: 然后说说我们的一些失败。
cues.en: And then some of our failures.

cues.zh: 我们创办了一家叫Z.com的公司，是一家在线娱乐公司。
cues.en: We started a company called Z.com, it was an online entertainment company.

cues.zh: 我们当时特别兴奋——
cues.en: We were so excited about it --

cues.zh: 我们融到了足够的钱，有很好的商业模式，
cues.en: we raised enough money, we had a great business model,

cues.zh: 甚至还签下了非常厉害的好莱坞人才加入公司。
cues.en: we even signed incredibly great Hollywood talent to join the company.

cues.zh: 但1999到2000年，宽带普及率太低了。
cues.en: But broadband penetration was too low in 1999-2000.

cues.zh: 以前在线看视频太难了，
cues.en: It was too hard to watch video content online,

cues.zh: 你得在浏览器里装编解码器，折腾一大堆东西，
cues.en: you had to put codecs in your browser and do all this stuff,

cues.zh: 这家公司最终在2003年倒闭了。
cues.en: and the company eventually went out of business in 2003.

cues.zh: 仅仅两年后，
cues.en: Just two years later,

cues.zh: 当Adobe Flash解决了编解码器的问题，
cues.en: when the codec problem was solved by Adobe Flash

cues.zh: 当美国宽带普及率超过50%时，
cues.en: and when broadband penetration crossed 50 percent in America,

cues.zh: YouTube的时机堪称完美。
cues.en: YouTube was perfectly timed.

cues.zh: 想法很棒，但时机好得难以置信。
cues.en: Great idea, but unbelievable timing.

cues.zh: 事实上，YouTube刚起步时甚至没有商业模式。
cues.en: In fact, YouTube didn't even have a business model when it first started.

cues.zh: 甚至都不能确定它能不能做成。
cues.en: It wasn't even certain that that would work out.

cues.zh: 但那个时机真是妙到毫巅。
cues.en: But that was beautifully, beautifully timed.

cues.zh: 所以总结来说，我想说的是，
cues.en: So what I would say, in summary,

cues.zh: 执行力当然非常重要。
cues.en: is execution definitely matters a lot.

cues.zh: 想法也很重要。
cues.en: The idea matters a lot.

cues.zh: 但时机可能更重要。
cues.en: But timing might matter even more.

cues.zh: 而真正评估时机的最好方法，
cues.en: And the best way to really assess timing

cues.zh: 就是认真去看消费者是否真的准备好了，
cues.en: is to really look at whether consumers are really ready

cues.zh: 迎接你要提供给他们的一切。
cues.en: for what you have to offer them.

cues.zh: 说实话，
cues.en: And to be really, really honest about it,

cues.zh: 不要对所看到的结果自欺欺人，
cues.en: not be in denial about any results that you see,

cues.zh: 因为如果你热爱某件事，就想推动它前进，
cues.en: because if you have something you love, you want to push it forward,

cues.zh: 但在时机这个因素上，你必须非常非常诚实。
cues.en: but you have to be very, very honest about that factor on timing.

cues.zh: 正如我之前所说，
cues.en: As I said earlier,

cues.zh: 我认为创业公司能改变世界，让世界变得更美好。
cues.en: I think startups can change the world and make the world a better place.

cues.zh: 我希望这些见解
cues.en: I hope some of these insights

cues.zh: 能帮你把成功率稍微提高一点，
cues.en: can maybe help you have a slightly higher success ratio,

cues.zh: 从而让伟大的东西来到这个世界，
cues.en: and thus make something great come to the world

cues.zh: 否则它就不会出现。
cues.en: that wouldn't have happened otherwise.

cues.zh: 非常感谢，你们是很棒的听众。
cues.en: Thank you very much, you've been a great audience.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
